title: LEEP (cervical cone procedure)
what: Using a thin wire loop, the doctor removes a small cone-shaped piece of the cervix. It is sent to the lab, and the abnormal tissue is removed at the same time.
why: When smears and a biopsy show abnormal cells on the cervix that need to be removed and studied.
duration: the procedure usually takes 15 to 30 minutes, and you usually go home the same day; lab results come in 1 to 3 weeks
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
Allergy to painkillers or numbing medicine
If you plan a pregnancy. This matters for how much tissue is removed

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: You usually need smears, a colposcopy, a biopsy, and blood tests. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: It is usually done in the first days after your period ends. Check with your doctor.

prepare.title: Numbing
prepare.text: Most often with local numbing, sometimes under brief anesthesia. With anesthesia, no food for 6 hours. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Your decision
prepare.text: Your doctor will explain why it is done and what happens after. You sign a consent form.

bring: Someone to take you home, if you have anesthesia
steps: You sit in the gynecological chair
A pad is stuck on your thigh. It is needed for the device to work safely
The doctor inserts a speculum, cleans the cervix, and numbs it with a shot
A thin loop removes a small piece of tissue. It takes a few minutes
The area is sealed so it does not bleed
The tissue is sent to the lab
feel: The shots in the cervix are briefly unpleasant
Period-like cramping low in the belly
Sometimes your heart beats faster from the medicine in the shot. This passes quickly
after: Discharge, bloody at first and then dark, usually lasts 2 to 4 weeks
No sex, tampons, baths, pools, or heavy exercise, usually for about 4 weeks
Your doctor will explain the lab results
Follow-up smears are usually done after a few months
red_flags: Bleeding heavier than a heavy period: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or bad-smelling discharge: see a doctor urgently
Severe pain low in the belly that painkillers do not ease

faq.q: Can I have a baby after LEEP?
faq.a: Usually yes. Sometimes extra monitoring is needed in pregnancy. Tell your doctor you had LEEP.
LEEP is done to remove abnormal cells before they become dangerous. The lab results will give the exact answer.
The cervix is numbed. You usually feel period-like cramping.

reminders.text: LEEP procedure tomorrow. Bring your test results and pads. If you have anesthesia, eat only until the time the clinic gave you.
